title: Customer Desk Training: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Billing Adjustments and Goodwill Credits
content:
Training material for the customer desk on adjustment credits to Fire & Smoke Mitigation charge lines: billing-error credits, duplicate-line credits and goodwill credits.

## The rule studied

> The job must be in cleaning complete or invoiced status when an adjustment credit is posted. A billing-error credit equals the amount charged less the amount the tier's rate and the recorded quantity produce; a duplicate-line credit equals the full amount of a repeated line. A billing-error or duplicate-line credit may be posted only when the customer raises the dispute no later than the dispute window after the final invoice was issued on this job. The dispute window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the job's invoice date, and a dispute raised on the last day of the window is in time; on a job not yet invoiced the window has not started and the dispute is always in time. Goodwill credits on one job may not exceed the tier's goodwill credit cap in total. A goodwill request above the remaining cap is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy. Each charge line takes at most one adjustment credit.

## Questions and answers on the rule

Q1. In which job statuses may an adjustment credit be posted?
Only in cleaning complete or invoiced status. A job that is dispatched, authorized, in cleaning, closed or cancelled takes no adjustment credit.

Q2. How large is a billing-error credit?
The amount charged on the line less the amount that the tier's rate times the recorded quantity produces. Hypothetical line: a line charged at 250.00 where the tier's rate and the recorded quantity produce 210.00 takes a billing-error credit of 40.00.

Q3. How large is a duplicate-line credit?
The full amount of the repeated line. A hypothetical line of 96.00 booked twice for the same item takes a duplicate-line credit of 96.00 on the repeated line.

Q4. How many adjustment credits can one charge line take?
At most one, whatever the reason.

## The dispute window

A billing-error or duplicate-line credit may be posted only when the customer raises the dispute no later than the dispute window after the final invoice was issued on this job. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the job's invoice date; the last day of the window is in time.

| Job and dispute date | In time? |
|---|---|
| Job not yet invoiced, any date | yes: the window has not started |
| Invoiced job, dispute on the day after the invoice date (day 1 of the window) | yes |
| Invoiced job, dispute on the last day of the window | yes |
| Invoiced job, dispute on the day after the last day of the window | no |

Hypothetical calendar: an invoice dated 1 March under a hypothetical window of 30 calendar days opens the window on 2 March; its last day is 31 March. A dispute raised on 31 March is in time; one raised on 1 April is not, and no billing-error or duplicate-line credit may then be posted.

The window is the tier's dispute window and is read from the job's own tier.

## Goodwill credits

Goodwill credits on one job may not exceed the tier's goodwill credit cap in total. The total counted is every goodwill credit already posted on the job. A goodwill request above the remaining cap is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy. The dispute window is a condition of billing-error and duplicate-line credits; the rule ties goodwill credits to the cap.

| Hypothetical cap | Goodwill already posted on the job | Remaining cap | Request | Under the rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250.00 | 180.00 | 70.00 | 60.00 | within the remaining cap |
| 250.00 | 180.00 | 70.00 | 70.00 | within the remaining cap, the total reaching the cap exactly |
| 250.00 | 180.00 | 70.00 | 90.00 | above the remaining cap: handed to a human representative as not covered by policy |
